transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-12-11
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Priya Anand (CEO), Alex Chen (CTO), Marco Ruiz (VP Eng), Sara Patel (Head People), Jordan Li (CFO), Emily Torres (Prod), Devon Park (Platform) + ~80 all-hands listeners (muted)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Year-end engineering and GTM priorities reviewed; focus on cost controls, reliability, and select growth bets.
- Immediate actions: freeze non-critical hiring, run infra cost SLO analysis, finalize Q1 priorities.
- Open Q&A on performance, Private deployments, and holiday on-call coverage.

Topics:
- Company performance and revenue pulse
- Q1 priorities and tradeoffs
- Cost/latency engineering work and Redwood Optimize suggestions
- Hiring posture and limited exceptions
- Holiday on-call and incident posture
- Ops and security reminders for Private deployments

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Priya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, on a, on a Thursday afternoon. I, I want to keep this tight — we've got about an hour — we're, we're doing a year-end helmbrief and priority deconflict. So first, quick state; Jordan, you want to kick us off with the revenue pulse?

[00:00:18] Jordan: Yeah sure, um so headline — revenue is slightly above plan for Q4, uh, mostly from Hosted API usage, we saw a couple of big spikes from enterprise pilots. Gross margin is, is tighter than expected because of higher GPU spot prices late November, so our unit economics slipped. I've put three scenarios in the deck I shared — plan, downside, upside — and I'll, I'll email the full numbers after.

[00:00:45] Priya: Okay, thanks. The important bit there is we have headroom this quarter but we need to, um, be conservative for Q1. Marco, from infra, what's the risk picture?

[00:00:55] Marco: Yeah so two things — reliability incidents have been low but we did see one prolonged reclaim event on Dedicated late last month when a region had a provider preemption cascade, and the fallback policy took a while to spin up compatible nodes. We've traced it to some orchestration race in the autoscaler and a subtle kernel mismatch in a quantized path. We have the postmortem draft.

[00:01:22] Alex: Quick clarifier — the kernel mismatch was in the int8 path for a small model family, not universal, right?

[00:01:28] Marco: Yeah correct. It was the quantized runtime switch for some open models we onboarded; the runtime selected a kernel optimized for different token widths, which caused slightly higher memory use and then the autoscaler misjudged.

[00:01:40] Priya: So mitigation is — short term, can we add a guardrail to prevent the autoscaler from aggregating those requests into a single bucket?

[00:01:47] Marco: Yup, we're rolling a flag that forces per-variant capacity isolation for the next two weeks, and Alex's team will push a microfix to the kernel selector. That should reduce surface area.

[00:01:57] [Speaker 2 / audience low]: (mumbled) what about KV cash? I think I saw something about that in the post...

[00:02:03] Devon: Sorry that was me — KV cache, yeah, the prefix caching had a stale entry that prolonged cold starts for a small subset of sessions, that's also in the postmortem.

[00:02:12] Priya: Okay good. On the product and go-to-market side — Emily?

[00:02:16] Emily: We closed a couple of pilot deals around Redwood Optimize — customers liked batching suggestions and quantization recs. But in demos we keep getting the same question: "how do you measure quality regressions when we change quantization profiles?" We need clearer eval artifacts and a short guide.

[00:02:34] Alex: We do have an eval harness but it's not packaged for sales, so DevRel is working on a reproducible notebook. I'll push a prioritized checklist for the next release.

[00:02:44] Priya: Great. Shifting to the higher-level ask — Q1. I'm proposing three company-level priorities: 1) reliability & predictable SLAs, 2) cost efficiency to defend margins, 3) product motions that enable land-and-expand (Optimize + Observability). Thoughts?

[00:03:03] Marco: Those map well to eng. For reliability we should target two SLOs: P99 latency band and model-serving availability per region. For cost efficiency, engineering will run a top-3 levers analysis — batching, KV cache hit-rate improvement, and instance right-sizing/quantization.

[00:03:20] Jordan: From finance, I want to be explicit — if we hit the top-3 levers by mid Q1 we stay on plan. If not, we need to reduce non-critical spend which includes some hiring buckets.

[00:03:32] Sara: On hiring — we're instituting a temporary hiring pause for non-customer facing ICs effective 12/20, with a small exceptions process. I'll circulate the form. We still need to fill critical roles tied to strategic bets — so exceptions can be made with leadership sign-off.

[00:03:48] Priya: Yep. We will keep customer-facing and security/compliance roles exempt. Speaking of security — quick reminder on Private deployments and VPC onboarding: audits are due for a subset of customers in January. Alex?

[00:04:01] Alex: Security & compliance team updated the SOC2 evidence collection playbook — it's on the confluence page. For private deployments, make sure KMS integration is tested; if you're owning a customer POC, tag the ticket as 'private-deploy-check'. We also improved logging retention toggles for on-prem customers.

[00:04:18] [00:04:18] Audience Q: Will we be expanding regions next year?

[00:04:21] Priya: Short answer — yes, but slower. We will prioritize APAC region after we stabilize cost at current regions. Jordan, cost to add a region?

[00:04:29] Jordan: Material, because of minimum committed instances and egress considerations. We can, we can run a scenario with 1) light presence vs 2) full capacity and decide.

[00:04:39] Marco: Also we need to validate some model latency profiles in APAC for heavy token workloads — we've seen higher tail latency on some architectures at long sequences.

[00:04:48] Priya: Okay next — product launches and GTM timeline. Emily, quick bullets?

[00:04:52] Emily: We're shifting the Redwood Optimize feature set into a beta for early customers Feb 1. The console UX improvements will be staggered — the cost-understanding dashboard first, then per-model rollout controls. We'll need docs and a short demo kit for sales.

[00:05:07] Alex: On the runtime side, we have a low-risk path to reduce per-token cost via a new batching scheduler that preserves latency SLOs; it's a Q1 engineering effort but high impact if we get it right.

[00:05:20] Priya: Good. OK let's open the floor for 10 minutes of questions. Please use the raise hand, we'll call on folks.

[00:05:28] [00:05:28] Question (All-hands): How will the hiring pause impact ongoing projects?

[00:05:33] Sara: Short answer — we will triage projects into green/amber/red. Green keeps hiring, amber gets reviewed, red paused. Team leads will get the triage template and meet with my team this week.

[00:05:44] [00:05:44] Question (All-hands): Any plan for year-end bonuses or comp adjustments?

[00:05:49] Jordan: We're finalizing comp cycles — assuming no major downside in December we'll do the standard bonus run but we might shift some of the larger discretionary pools to early Q2 if downside plays out. We'll communicate specifics by EOD Friday.

[00:06:01] Priya: Real talk — I know a hiring pause creates stress, but I want to emphasize it's temporary and targeted. We're trying to balance runway and growth. We will be transparent and give teams time to plan.

[00:06:12] [00:06:12] Question (All-hands, muffled): On-call over holidays, what's coverage look like?

[00:06:16] Marco: We'll keep the usual rotations but with a smaller on-call footprint — paging policies tightened for certain non-critical alerts. There's an incentive time-off swap for folks who cover critical days; Sara's team will follow up.

[00:06:27] Priya: Cool. I want to surface three things before we wrap: one, prioritize the infra guardrails Marco mentioned; two, Alex/Eng own the cost SLO analysis; three, People will publish hiring exception process. Also Jordan will finalize the budget scenarios.

[00:06:45] Alex: Quick note on the kernel/quant path — we should add a short-term toggle at deploy time so we can revert quant kernels by variant. That will help immediate safety for customer deploys.

[00:06:56] Marco: We're going to ship the guardrail flag tomorrow in canary and monitor error rates.

[00:07:01] Priya: Great. Final items — I want each org lead to send a 1-page plan for Q1 that lists one primary metric, two risks, and three actions. Please have that to me by Monday 12/15.

[00:07:14] Emily: We'll also produce a short one pager for sales: "How Redwood Optimize affects cost and quality".

[00:07:20] [00:07:20] Closing remarks, Priya: Thanks for the hustle this year — proud of the team. We'll reconvene in January for a more detailed roadmap session. Happy holidays to those celebrating.

[00:07:31] End of meeting notes:
- Docs referenced: Q4 revenue deck (link in slack), postmortem draft (confluence), hiring exception form (hr confluence).
- Shared artifacts: will email the Q1 priorities template and a recorded version of this all-hands.

[00:07:45] Misc transcription quirks: occasional speaker mislabels, background chatter, 'KV cash' mis-transcription in one segment, 'int8' sometimes spoken as 'in tee eight' in the transcript.

Action recap (verbatim):
- Marco: produce 2-slide infra risk & mitigation summary by 2025-12-18.
- Alex: latency/cost tradeoff slide for Dedicated vs Hosted by 2025-12-17.
- Sara: publish hiring exception form and timeline by 2025-12-16.
- Jordan: revised budget scenarios by 2025-12-19.
